title: Hyperscale Model Feature Scout & Competitive Synthesis
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Objective: Rapidly surface features and capability deltas across hyperscale and open LLMs (short-context performance, streaming stability, tool-calling semantics, KV-cache behavior, quant-compatibility) and translate findings into prioritized product levers (routing, model variants, tooling, pricing).

Scope: A two-week reconnaissance and synthesis covering 6 vendor models + 8 community/open variants. Deliverables: 1) a concise evidence matrix that maps feature deltas to product impact (latency/cost/quality tradeoffs); 2) a signal deck for GTM and solutions teams; 3) a small set of experiment recipes for Redwood Optimize to validate cost/perf gains.

Approach: Combine automated microbenchmarks (latency P50/95 across contexts), curated prompt probes for failure modes, and a short set of customer scenario replays (RAG short-doc retrieval, multi-step API chains). Cross-annotate each signal with provenance, reproducibility score, and suggested remediation or exploitation path (eg. pin model variant, add fallback route, recommend quant profile).

Why now: Recent releases from hyperscalers introduced subtle semantic changes (tool-calling alignment, streaming chunking behaviour) that could materially affect Redwood’s fallback policies and cost calculators. This ticket focuses on surfacing actionable differences and short experiments rather than exhaustive sweeping analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence matrix completed for 14 target models with reproducibility score for each signal
Three concrete product recommendations with estimated unit economics impact (tokens, latency) and implementation owner
Signal deck (PDF/Confluence) shared with GTM, Runtime, and Optimize teams and reviewed in sync
Two experiment recipes pushed to experiments repo with clear success metrics and owners
